result.summary: This PR fixes a bug where the wallet descriptor-cache loader (WALLETDESCRIPTORCACHE/WALLETDESCRIPTORLHCACHE) deserializes a length-prefixed vector but then calls CExtPubKey::Decode with a fixed BIP32_EXTKEY_SIZE, causing an out-of-bounds read on short records (confirmed as an ASan container-overflow). The first commit adds a length check that rejects malformed records with DBErrors::CORRUPT, matching how other corrupt records are handled, plus a unit test. The second commit, added after maintainer feedback, replaces CExtKey/CExtPubKey's pointer-based Encode/Decode/EncodeWithVersion/DecodeWithVersion with stream-based Serialize/Unserialize and routes base58, PSBT, and wallet cache code through them, so the expected length is enforced by the stream at every call site rather than by ad hoc checks. The on-disk cache format, base58 encodings, and PSBT xpub encodings are unchanged.
result.problem: A crafted or corrupted wallet database can contain a descriptor-cache record with a short serialized xpub; loading it currently reads 74 bytes from a shorter buffer, an out-of-bounds read caught by ASan. This affects anyone whose wallet file is loaded by bitcoind, since the loader currently has no size check before decoding.

open_concerns: molnard's suggestion to add a scope guard / secure buffer for the temporary key bytes in CExtKey::Unserialize was implemented (switched to a secure_allocator-backed buffer).
winterrdog's suggestion to also simplify wallet_load_descriptors with ASSERT_DEBUG_LOG was deferred by the author as out of scope, not disputed.
resolved_concerns: achow101 initially pushed for a broader Serialize/Unserialize refactor rather than a local fix; author implemented it in a second commit and achow101 ACKed the result.
32-bit ARM CI array-bounds false positive from chained stream operators, fixed by splitting the statements per winterrdog's suggestion.

molnard requested negative-path tests for CExtKey/CExtPubKey deserialization (short streams, over-long streams, invalid content); author added bip32_deserialize_invalid covering all cases and molnard ACKed.

result.card: This PR fixes a wallet-loader bug where a descriptor-cache record with a short serialized xpub causes CExtPubKey::Decode to read past the end of a vector, confirmed as an ASan container-overflow. Beyond the local size check, the author added a second commit replacing CExtKey/CExtPubKey's pointer-based Encode/Decode with stream-based Serialize/Unserialize at achow101's request, so every call site (base58, PSBT, wallet cache) now has its expected length enforced by the stream itself, with on-disk formats and encodings unchanged. Both achow101 and molnard reviewed substantively and ACKed the final commit after their requests (more negative-path tests, a secure_allocator-backed temporary buffer, fixing a 32-bit ARM CI false positive) were addressed. The PR currently shows CI failed, with the most recent comment noting a maintainer must approve the workflow to run it. No dependency on other PRs, though it conflicts with the unrelated open PR #36133 (multipath descriptor storage).
